Replace the passive target with a close-packed array of **1 cm × 1 cm × 1 cm polystyrene scintillator cubes** read out by **silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs)** via wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibers along three orthogonal axes.
- 1 cm cubing gives ~1.5 cm minimum detectable track length → captures 60 MeV protons (range ~2.5 cm in scintillator, so ~2 cubes minimum)
- dE/dx from pulse height in each cube enables proton/pion separation

**Mitigation — use carbon-rich or hydrogen-free scintillator medium:**
- Replace polystyrene cubes with **lithium fluoride (LiF) or borosilicate glass** scintillator tiles: near-zero hydrogen
- Alternatively: **carbon-loaded liquid scintillator** with minimal H content is difficult
- Most practical: **graphite (carbon) blocks** as passive absorber interspersed with thin scintillator planes (see below), or use **gadolinium-doped glass scintillator cubes**

Preferred implementation: **borosilicate glass scintillator cubes** (Corning-type, ~SiO₂·B₂O₃·Na₂O, hydrogen nucleon fraction <0.1%) read out with SiPMs via cerium-doped glass fiber — zero hydrogen issue satisfied.

**Hydrogen content:** Scintillator panels are outside the fiducial active target volume and do not count toward the nucleon composition of the analysis target.
